**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the

and assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with spectral
projection-valued measure $E_H$ and flow
$U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]). Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) Symmetry of the dynamics.** A **symmetry of the declared dynamics**, or
simply a **symmetry**, is a unitary operator $S\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}}),\qquad S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S\ \text{ on }D(H_{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The reading is the model's: a symmetry is a unitary that preserves the assigned
energy domain and commutes with the assigned energy operator on that domain;
the equivalent formulation by commutation with the flow $U(t)$, and the
concomitant conservation statements, are proved results of this page and are
not part of this definition. Neither the energy operator nor its potential or
coupling terms are assumed to possess any symmetry here.

**(c) Unitary symmetry group.** A **unitary symmetry group** of the declared
system is a group $G$ together with a map $g\mapsto S_g$ from $G$ into the
unitary operators of $H$ such that $S_e=I$, $S_{gh}=S_gS_h$ and every $S_g$ is
a symmetry in the sense of (b). When $G$ carries a topology, the group is
**strongly continuous** when $g\mapsto S_g f$ is continuous for every
$f\in H$; for the one-parameter case the concrete condition is that of
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]. The model's standard
candidate spatial symmetry groups and additional unitary symmetry actions,
which must satisfy clause (b) before any one of them is called a symmetry,
include:

1. the **spatial translations** $T_a$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c),
   forming the group $\mathbb R^{3}$, with generator data supplied by
   [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d);
2. the **spatial rotations** $U(R)$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]], forming the group $SO(3)$
   with its Euclidean topology, and their coordinate one-parameter subgroups,
   whose generators are the operators $L_{i}$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]];
3. the **spatial parity** action $\Pi$ of
   [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], forming the two-element group
   $\{I,\Pi\}$;
4. in the **spinless scalar case** $H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the
   **gauge phase multipliers** $G_{\chi}(t)$. No action on an internal factor
   is defined here. Given an open interval $I$, a real Borel
   function $\chi:\mathbb R^{3}\times I\to\mathbb R$ with unit
   $\mathrm{J\,s\,C^{-1}}$, a charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$ with unit C,
   and $\hbar>0$ with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, define
   $$\bigl(G_{\chi}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\!\bigl(iq\chi(x,t)/\hbar\bigr)\psi(x)\quad\text{for almost every }x,\qquad \psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C).$$
   For each fixed $t$, this is a unitary operator. The real coefficients in
   the defining power series give
   $\overline{\exp(i\theta)}=\exp(-i\theta)$ for real $\theta$; by absolute
   convergence, the Cauchy product for $\exp(i\theta)\exp(-i\theta)$ groups
   the coefficient of degree $k$ as
   $\frac1{k!}\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}(-1)^{k-j}$; the finite sum is
   $(1-1)^k$, hence is $1$ for $k=0$ and $0$ for $k\ge1$. Therefore
   $|\exp(i\theta)|=1$ and the inverse multiplier is
   $\exp\!\bigl(-iq\chi(\cdot,t)/\hbar\bigr)$. This definition asserts only its action on
   $L^{2}$; it assumes no regularity of $\chi$ and does not imply preservation
   of an unbounded energy domain. The gauge-covariance result treats only the
   additional regularity class stated by the prescribed-coupling postulate.

**(d) One-parameter symmetry group and generator.** A **one-parameter symmetry
group** is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto S_t=e^{-itA/\hbar}$ with every $S_t$ a symmetry in the sense of (b),
where $A$ is the self-adjoint **generator** furnished by Stone's theorem
([[thm-stone-one-parameter-unitary-groups]]); its declared unit is that of the
spectral coordinate of $A$. When $S_t=U(R_i(t))$ for a coordinate rotation
subgroup, $A$ is the operator $L_i$ above; when
$S_t=T_{te_j}$, $A$ is the momentum component $P_j$ in the reading of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).

**(e) Conserved sharp observables.** Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp
observable of the framework ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]).
It is **conserved along the flow** when its outcome law is independent of time
in every preparation: for every preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]) and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}.$$
The conserved object is thus the outcome law of the assigned observable — a
probability measure on the Borel sets — and, where the moments exist, its
moments; the definition does not say that a single numerical value is revealed
at each time, and it identifies no laboratory quantity with the pair $(A,u_A)$.

**(f) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the vocabulary of this page within
P1, P2 and P4 and the cited readings. They assert no symmetry of any concrete
model: whether $T_a$, $U(R)$ or $\Pi$ is a symmetry of a given bounded-potential
dynamics is decided by the conditional results of this page. The gauge
definition asserts only an $L^{2}$ unitary; a symmetry claim must separately
verify the energy-domain and commutation conditions of clause (b). Antiunitary
symmetries, superselection sectors, symmetries of preparations as opposed to
dynamics, and any empirical claim about which symmetries a laboratory system
possesses are outside this definition. The
parameter $a$ of a translation has the unit of length $u_H$ of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the rotation group and parity
act on the spatial factor only, in the readings of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]], and the prescribed-coupling reading is
that of [[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-magnetic-schrodinger-operator]].

matrices $\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e). Then:

(a) for every $W\in SU(2)$ the operator $U_{s}(W)$ is unitary, with
$U_{s}(I)=\mathrm{id}$ and $U_{s}(W_{1}W_{2})=U_{s}(W_{1})U_{s}(W_{2})$ for
all $W_{1},W_{2}\in SU(2)$, and $W\mapsto U_{s}(W)$ is strongly continuous
([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]);

(b) $\rho(A_{i}(t))=R_{i}(t)$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$ and every $i$, and
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary
group ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]);

(c) the operators $L_{i}$ and $S_{i}$ strongly commute (their spectral
projection-valued measures commute;
[[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]],
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]), the sum $J_{i}:=L_{i}+S_{i}$ with
domain $D(J_{i}):=D(L_{i})$ is self-adjoint, and
$$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
moreover for $W\in SU(2)$ one has the conjugation identities including
domains
$$U_{s}(W)Q_{j}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lj}Q_{l},\qquad U_{s}(W)P_{k}U_{s}(W)^{-1}=\sum_{l=1}^{3}\rho(W)_{lk}P_{l},$$
where $Q_{j},P_{k}$ are the componentwise position and momentum operators of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a) and
$\rho(W)_{lj}$ are the matrix entries of the transported cover in the standard basis; the sums mean the maximal directional realizations $Q(\rho(W)e_j)$ and $P(\rho(W)e_k)$ of [[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]] clause (b), with domains $U_s(W)D(Q_j)$ and $U_s(W)D(P_k)$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is a mathematical statement about the
finite-dimensional spin representation and the componentwise rotation action;
it asserts no physical interpretation, no measurement, no dynamics and no
value of $\hbar$, $s$ or $W$. The spatial action enters only through
$U(R)=U(\rho(W))$ and the internal action only through $M_{s}(W)$; no action
on a second spatial or internal factor is introduced.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $K$ be a
self-adjoint operator on $\mathcal H$ with spectral projection-valued measure
$E=E_K$ on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and put
$U(t):=e^{-itK/\hbar}=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE(\lambda)$ for
$\hbar>0$, the strongly continuous unitary group generated by $-iK/\hbar$
([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]],
[[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]).

(a) If a bounded operator $B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ satisfies
$BE(C)=E(C)B$ for every Borel set $C\subseteq\mathbb R$, then
$BU(t)=U(t)B$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$.

(a') If a bounded self-adjoint operator $S$ satisfies $SK\subseteq KS$ — that
is $S(Kx)=K(Sx)$ for every $x\in D(K)$ — then $SU(t)=U(t)S$ for every $t$.

(b) Let $F$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space
$(Y,\Sigma)$ with $F(S)E(C)=E(C)F(S)$ for all $S\in\Sigma$ and all Borel
$C\subseteq\mathbb R$. Then:

(i) $F(S)U(t)=U(t)F(S)$ for all $t$ and $S$;

(ii) for every density operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$ — a self-adjoint
positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$
([[def-trace-class-operator]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)) —
the numbers $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F(S))$ are independent of $t$:
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(U(t)\rho U(t)^*F(S)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho F(S)\bigr) \qquad(t\in\mathbb R,\ S\in\Sigma);$$

(iii) for every unit vector $\psi\in\mathcal H$ and every $S$,
$\|F(S)U(t)\psi\|^2=\|F(S)\psi\|^2$ for all $t$;

(c) applying (b) with $F=E$: for every density operator $\rho$ the energy law
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(C))$ is independent of $t$, for every unit $\psi$
the law $\|E(C)U(t)\psi\|^2=\|E(C)\psi\|^2$ is independent of $t$, and if
$\psi\in D(K)$ then both existing scalar moments are conserved:
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^k\,dE_{K,U(t)\psi}(\lambda) =\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^k\,dE_{K,\psi}(\lambda),\qquad k=1,2,$$
with the integrals finite at $t=0$ and equal to $\langle K\psi,\psi\rangle$
and $\|K\psi\|^2$ respectively; moments that are infinite at $t=0$ remain
outside the assertion;

(d) if $K\psi=\lambda\psi$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and unit
$\psi\in D(K)$, then $U(t)\psi=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ for every $t$, and
every $S\mapsto\|F(S)\psi\|^2$ of (b) agrees with
$S\mapsto\|F(S)U(t)\psi\|^2$.

No equilibration, relaxation or convergence of the law of an arbitrary state
is asserted, and no moment beyond those finite at $t=0$ is claimed.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] for a declared isolated
system with state space $H$, assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$
and flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]); use the symmetry vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]]. Assume the
Axiom of Choice, the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Dependent
Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(A,u_A)$ be an assigned sharp observable of the
system with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and put
$W(s):=e^{-isA/\hbar}$. Then the following are equivalent:

(i) $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$;

(ii) $E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)$ for all Borel sets $B,C\subseteq\mathbb R$;

(iii) $U(t)D(A)=D(A)$ and $U(t)AU(t)^{*}=A$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$.

When they hold:

(a) **Conserved law.** The outcome law of $(A,u_A)$ is time-independent: for
every preparation $\rho$, every Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and every $t$,
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho(0)}(B),\qquad \mu^{A}_{\psi(t)}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\psi(0)}(B)\ \text{for a unit }\psi\ \text{with }\psi(t)=U(t)\psi(0).$$

(b) **Conserved moments.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ is a unit vector, then the mean and
the second moment of the law of $A$ in the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ are
finite and independent of $t$, with time-zero values
$\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; if a moment is infinite at
$t=0$, no equality of finite quantities is claimed.

(c) **Unitary symmetries of the dynamics.** If a unitary operator $S$ is a
symmetry in the sense of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]], that is
$S\,D(H_{\mathrm{op}})=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$ and
$S\,H_{\mathrm{op}}=H_{\mathrm{op}}\,S$, then $S\,U(t)=U(t)\,S$ for every $t$;
if in addition $S$ is self-adjoint, then the outcome law of the assigned sharp
observable $(S,u_S)$ with its spectral coordinate unit is time-independent in
every preparation.

(d) **Status and exclusions.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2 and P4
and the cited mathematics. Its symmetry hypothesis is the strong commutation of
the flows or, equivalently, of the spectral measures, not a formal commutator
identity on a small domain; no definite value of a conserved observable is
asserted; no converse from the constancy of laws to the commutation conditions
is claimed for unbounded $A$; and no concrete model potential, apparatus,
measurement record or empirical result is introduced.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ and scalar measures $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For a unit vector $\psi\in H$ write $\mu^{A}_{\psi}:=\mu^{A}_{T_{\psi,\psi}}$ for the scalar law of the pure state $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b). Then:

(a) **Second moment.** $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}$ if $\psi\in D(A)$, and the integral equals $+\infty$ if $\psi\notin D(A)$; thus the second moment of the scalar law is finite exactly on $D(A)$.

(b) **Mean.** $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ if and only if $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$; in that case the mean $m(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)$ is finite and real, and if $\psi\in D(A)$ then $m(\psi)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$.

(c) **Variance.** If $\psi\in D(A)$ and $m:=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$, then
$$\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^{2}-m^{2}=\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}\ge0 ;$$
if in addition $\psi\in D(A^{2})$, that is $\psi\in D(A)$ and $A\psi\in D(A)$, then $\|(A-m)\psi\|^{2}=\langle A^{2}\psi,\psi\rangle-\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle^{2}$.

(d) **States.** Let $\rho$ be a density operator with expansion $\rho=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$, $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, $(u_n)$ orthonormal. In every weighted sum below, a term with $w_n=0$ is defined to be zero before any component integral is evaluated; equivalently, sum only over $n$ with $w_n>0$. This convention also applies to signed component means, which need not exist at zero-weight indices. Then for every Borel function $g\ge0$
$$\int_{\mathbb R}g\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_n\int_{\mathbb R}g\,dE_{A,u_n}\in[0,\infty],$$
so the mean of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is finite if and only if $\sum_nw_n\int|\lambda|\,dE_{A,u_n}<\infty$, and then it equals $\sum_nw_n\int\lambda\,dE_{A,u_n}$. For the second moment, put $M_n:=\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,u_n}$, so $M_n=\|Au_n\|^{2}$ when $u_n\in D(A)$ and $M_n=+\infty$ otherwise; a zero weight contributes zero. Then $\int\lambda^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}=\sum_nw_nM_n\in[0,\infty]$. It is finite exactly when every $u_n$ with $w_n>0$ lies in $D(A)$ and $\sum_{n:w_n>0}w_n\|Au_n\|^{2}<\infty$; componentwise domain membership alone does not ensure a finite second moment.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ and
$K$ be Hilbert spaces over the same field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H,K)$ be a compact operator ([[def-compact-linear-operator]])
with zero-padded singular-value sequence $(s_n(T))_{n\ge1}$
([[def-absolute-value-and-singular-values-of-a-compact-operator]]).

**Trace class.** The operator $T$ is **trace class** when
$$\sum_{n\ge1}s_n(T):=\sum_{m\in\mathbb N}s_{m+1}(T)<+\infty .$$
Thus the series in the zero-based convention of
[[def-series-and-absolute-convergence-in-a-normed-space]] is formed from the
explicit sequence $(s_{m+1}(T))_{m\in\mathbb N}$. In that case its **trace
norm** is
$$\|T\|_1:=\sum_{m\in\mathbb N}s_{m+1}(T)\in[0,+\infty),$$
and $\|T\|_1$ is also written $\|T\|_{\mathrm{tr}}$. The set of trace-class
operators $H\to K$ is written $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$.

**Immediate consequences.** Since $0\le s_n(T)\le s_1(T)=\|T\|$
([[def-absolute-value-and-singular-values-of-a-compact-operator]]), the terms
are nonnegative and $\|T\|_1\ge\|T\|\ge0$ whenever $T$ is trace class; the zero
operator is trace class with $\|0\|_1=0$. When $T$ has finite rank $r$ the
sequence is zero-padded, the series is the finite sum
$\sum_{n=1}^r s_n(T)=\sum_{\lambda>0}\lambda\dim_{\mathbb F} E_\lambda(|T|)$ over the finitely
many positive eigenvalues of $|T|$ counted with multiplicity ([[def-dimension]]),
and every finite-rank operator is compact
([[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]]) and therefore trace class; in particular every
operator with finite-dimensional range and every rank-one operator is trace
class. If $T$ has infinite rank then $s_n(T)>0$ for every $n$ and the series
$\sum_{n\ge1}s_n(T)$ converges in the summable case. By the necessary
condition for convergence of a scalar series ([[lem-nth-term-test]]), a
trace-class operator with infinite rank has $s_n(T)\to0$, hence
is a norm limit of finite-rank operators
([[thm-singular-value-decomposition-for-compact-operators]]).

**Choice accounting.** Trace class is defined through the singular values of
[[def-absolute-value-and-singular-values-of-a-compact-operator]], whose
construction uses $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the countable selection of finite
orthonormal bases of the eigenspaces of $|T|$ and the spectral theorem; no
Hilbert basis of the ambient space, and no stronger choice, is used here.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

derivations.claim: [Internal factors commute with the dynamics] Let $M$ be the fibrewise matrix action of a fixed matrix; by [F4] $M$ commutes with $P_{k}$ and with $M_{V}$ and preserves $W^{2,2}$, hence $MD(H_{V})\subseteq D(H_{V})$, $M(H_{V}\psi)=H_{V}(M\psi)$ for $\psi\in D(H_{V})$, and $MU(t)=U(t)M$ for every $t$: write $M=M_1+iM_2$ with $M_1=(M+M^*)/2$, $M_2=(M-M^*)/(2i)$ self-adjoint fibrewise matrix actions, apply the second part of [F4] to each, and add; in particular this applies to $M=M_{s}(A_{i}(t))$, to $M=S_{i}$ and to every bounded matrix action.

[Spatial rotations are symmetries] By the hypothesis $V\circ R^{-1}=V$ almost everywhere and [F2], every $U(R)$ is a symmetry of $H_{V}$, so $U(R)U(t)=U(t)U(R)$ for all $R,t$ and $U(R)D(H_{V})=D(H_{V})$; in particular this holds for the coordinate rotations $U(R_{i}(t))$.

[Lifted coordinate groups are symmetries] Fix $i$ and $t$; by [F3], $U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=U(R_{i}(t))M_{s}(A_{i}(t))$; by step 1.2 the first factor commutes with $U(u)$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$, and by step 1.1 the second factor does the same, so the product commutes with $U(u)$ for every $u$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$; combined with the group property and strong continuity of [F3], the family $t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group of symmetries, which is (a).

[Spin and orbital components] By step 1.1 applied to $M=S_{i}$, the bounded self-adjoint $S_{i}$ satisfies $S_{i}H_{V}\subseteq H_{V}S_{i}$, so [F4] gives $S_{i}U(t)=U(t)S_{i}$ for every $t$; applying [F5] with $A:=S_{i}$ (bounded, so $W(s)=e^{-isS_{i}/\hbar}$ commutes with $U$) gives the time-independence of the law of $S_{i}$ in every preparation, and by [F2] the law and moments of each $L_{i}$ are time-independent as well, which is (c).

[Total angular momentum conservation] By step 2.1 and [F3], the group $W(s):=e^{-isJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}=U_{s}(A_{i}(s))$ satisfies $W(s)U(t)=U(t)W(s)$ for all $s,t$ and preserves $D(H_{V})$; applying [F5] to the assigned sharp observable $(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ of [[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause (d) gives the time-independence of its outcome law in every preparation and, for a unit $\psi\in D(L_{i})=D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}})$, the conservation of the mean and second moment with the stated time-zero values, which is (b).

[Assembly and scope] Step 2.1 proves (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c); only the bounded-potential domain, the almost-everywhere rotational invariance and the lifted coordinate groups were used, no spin-dependent or singular potential, apparatus or empirical input entered, and the conserved object is the outcome law, which is the scope statement (d).
