Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $E_{A,x}(B):=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ be its scalar measures ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ say that $\lambda$ is an **eigenvalue** of $A$ when $Ax=\lambda x$ for some nonzero $x\in D(A)$, the domain-restricted reading of [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]. Then:

(a) The orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)=\{x\in D(A):Ax=\lambda x\}$; in particular $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$.

(b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, that is every self-adjoint positive trace-class $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(\{\lambda\}))$ is the weight that the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ assigns to the singleton $\{\lambda\}$: it vanishes for every $\rho$ whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and it equals $1$ for the pure state $T_{u,u}$ of every unit eigenvector $u\in\ker(A-\lambda)$.

(c) If $A$ has no eigenvalues at all, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every density operator $\rho$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$: the scalar law of every state carries no point mass, while its values on general Borel sets remain $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$.

Clauses (a)-(c) are mathematical statements about $A$, $E_A$ and the density operators; no physical interpretation of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is asserted here.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$. If $A$ has no eigenvalues, every preparation has an atomless outcome law: each singleton has probability zero, while $\mathbb R$ remains the outcome space and the law is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$ as in clause (d). Zero singleton probability does not exclude real point values as realizations of this law; it supplies no normalized exact-value eigenstate. A finite-resolution record is read through its declared Borel bin, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**(a) Adopted model and state space.** Adopt the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor
assigned as in the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Put $r:=2s+1$ and take
as the model's one-particle state space the complex Hilbert space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality almost everywhere, with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$
linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
Thus an element of $H_{s}$ is a class of functions, not a function, and
pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1
is $\ell^{-3/2}$ per component. P5 presents the same space as the completed
tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

**(b) Position and momentum.** The model's $j$-th position and $k$-th momentum
are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

**(c) Internal factor.** For $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^{r}$ of the spin assignment P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\hbar\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Momentum-space representative.** With $U^{(s)}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform
$$(\psi_{p})_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi_{l}(x)\,dx,$$
and its dimension is $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^{-3/2}$ per component
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

**(e) Frame reading.** The model's inertial frames are the global coordinate
charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. The transformation law of state
representatives under a change of inertial frame is a derived statement about
the model's operators and is established by the covariance theorems of this
page for translations and boosts; it is not an additional assumption of this
definition, and no Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) record the readings of P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the
terminology of this page and fix the objects used by its theorems. They assert
no time evolution beyond what the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 assigns
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv)), no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model and no
empirical result. Massless particles, relativistic matter, radiation, singular
or unbounded potentials and boundary or confined realizations are separate
model assumptions with their own domains and self-adjointness statements; none
is obtained from this definition.

**(a) State space.** Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] for a declared system of the declared massive-matter sector, with its assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. The **state space of the system in the model** is the set
$$D(H)=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}$$
of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]: the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $H$ of trace one. A **state** of the system is an element of $D(H)$; this is the geometry vocabulary for the general preparations of clause (iii) of the state postulate. The model's adopted assignment of a state to each preparation is not produced by this definition; it is the content of that postulate.

**(b) Pure and mixed states.** A state is **pure** when it is one of the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$, and **mixed** when it is not pure, as in [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the map
$$j:R(H)\to D(H),\qquad j([\psi])=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is a bijection of the ray space onto the set of pure states; and by clause (ii) of the state postulate the pure preparations are the unit rays of $H$, so the model's pure preparations are exactly its pure states.

**(c) State assigned to a state vector.** For a nonzero vector $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **state assigned to $\psi$** is the normalized rank-one operator
$$\widehat\rho(\psi)=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}\in D(H),$$
which by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; clause (ii) of the state postulate assigns the same operator to the pure preparation $[\psi]$. The zero vector is excluded here because $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ is defined only for $\psi\ne0$; no state is assigned to it, in agreement with the state postulate.

**(d) Mixtures and purity.** A **statistical mixture** of preparations with weights is the trace-norm convergent sum of clause (iii) of the state postulate; its value is the corresponding convex combination of states. The **purity** of a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})$, and by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]] a state is pure exactly when its purity equals $1$.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) record the readings of the state postulate in the geometry vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. The cited mathematical suppliers of the ray-to-state correspondence and of the purity criterion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is carried as a hypothesis of these readings. They adopt no assumption beyond the state postulate and that hypothesis, assert no dynamics, no probability law and no measurement model, and make no empirical claim: in particular, whether a given laboratory preparation is pure or mixed, and whether a given apparatus realizes a prescribed mixture, are physical identifications with uncertainty, governed by the preparation and apparatus assumptions of the framework, not consequences of this definition. Superselection restrictions and identical-particle symmetry sectors, where imposed, are separate assumptions by clause (v) of the state postulate and are not part of the state space fixed here.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

derivations.claim: [Bloch vector] Writing $v=(v_{1},v_{2})$ with $|v_{1}|^{2}+|v_{2}|^{2}=1$ and $z:=v_{1}\overline{v_{2}}$, the Pauli actions in [F1] and the inner product linear in the first argument give $\langle\sigma_{1}v,v\rangle=z+\overline z=2\operatorname{Re}z$, while $\langle\sigma_{2}v,v\rangle=-i\overline z+iz=i(z-\overline z)=-2\operatorname{Im}z$; also $\langle\sigma_{3}v,v\rangle=|v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2}$. Thus $\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_v$ is the vector of Pauli expectations, and $|\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_v|^{2}=4|v_{1}v_{2}|^{2}+(|v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2})^{2}=(|v_{1}|^{2}+|v_{2}|^{2})^{2}=1$.

[Directional law] For the product vector $\psi=f\otimes v$ and a unit $n$, the fibrewise projection acts as $P_{\pm}\psi=f\otimes\tfrac12(I\pm n\cdot\sigma)v$, so by [F2], $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\tfrac12(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)v,v\rangle)=\tfrac12(1\pm n\cdot\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v})$ using step 1.1; this is (i).

[Parametrized spinor] For $v=(e^{i\varphi}\cos(\theta/2),\sin(\theta/2))$ one has $v_{1}\overline{v_{2}}=e^{i\varphi}\cos(\theta/2)\sin(\theta/2)$, so $2\operatorname{Re}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}})=\sin\theta\cos\varphi$, $-2\operatorname{Im}(v_{1}\overline{v_{2}})=-\sin\theta\sin\varphi$ and $|v_{1}|^{2}-|v_{2}|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta/2)-\sin^{2}(\theta/2)=\cos\theta$; substituting $n=e_{3}$ and $n=e_{1}$ into step 2.1 gives the coordinate probabilities of (ii).

[Worked states] For $v=e_{1/2}$ the parametrization has $\theta=0$, so $\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}=(0,0,1)$ and step 2.1 gives $\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$, $\mu^{S_{3}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$ and $\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\tfrac12$; for $v=(e_{1/2}+e_{-1/2})/\sqrt2$ one has $\langle\boldsymbol\sigma\rangle_{v}=(1,0,0)$ by step 1.1, and step 2.1 with $n=e_{1}$ gives $\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{\hbar/2\})=1$ and $\mu^{S_{1}}_{\psi}(\{-\hbar/2\})=0$, which is (iii).

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $P_l$ be the Legendre polynomials of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-legendre-rodrigues-equation]], and for $l\in\mathbb N$ and $0\le m\le l$ define the
function $w_{lm}:(-1,1)\to\mathbb R$ by

$$w_{lm}(t):=(-1)^m(1-t^2)^{m/2}\,\frac{d^m}{dt^m}P_l(t),$$

where $(1-t^2)^{1/2}>0$ denotes the nonnegative square root. Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on
$S^2$ and let the angle coordinates be $\Phi(\theta,\varphi)=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$
([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]). The image of $\Phi$ is
$S^2\setminus C$, where $C:=\{(x,0,z)\in S^2:x\ge0\}$; $C$ is closed and $\sigma(C)=0$ by applying the integral identity of
[[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]] to its indicator. For $l\ge m\ge0$, define the representative
$\widetilde Y_{lm}:S^2\to\mathbb C$ on $S^2\setminus C$ by
$$\widetilde Y_{lm}(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)):=b_{lm}w_{lm}(\cos\theta)\frac{e^{im\varphi}}{\sqrt{2\pi}},$$
and on the cut $C$ by
$$\widetilde Y_{lm}(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta):=b_{lm}w_{lm}(\cos\theta)/\sqrt{2\pi}\qquad(0\le\theta\le\pi).$$
The limits at $\varphi=0$ and $2\pi$ agree because $m$ is an integer, and the endpoint values of $w_{lm}$ from (a) give the limits at the poles; hence $\widetilde Y_{lm}$ is continuous. For $1\le m\le l$ set
$\widetilde Y_{l,-m}:=(-1)^m\overline{\widetilde Y_{lm}}$, and write $Y_{lm}$ for the class of $\widetilde Y_{lm}$ in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$. Then:

(a) each $w_{lm}$ extends continuously to $[-1,1]$, with $w_{lm}(\pm1)=0$ when $m\ge1$, and on $(-1,1)$
it satisfies the associated Legendre equation
$$-\bigl((1-t^2)w_{lm}'\bigr)'+\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}w_{lm}=l(l+1)w_{lm}\qquad(-1<t<1),$$
equivalently $(1-t^2)w_{lm}''-2tw_{lm}'+\Bigl[l(l+1)-\frac{m^2}{1-t^2}\Bigr]w_{lm}=0$;

(b) for fixed $m\ge0$ the functions $w_{lm}$, $l\ge m$, are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2((-1,1),dt)$:
$\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}w_{km}\,dt=0$ for $k\ne l$; moreover $0<\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt<+\infty$;

(c) with $b_{lm}:=\bigl(\int_{-1}^1w_{lm}^2\,dt\bigr)^{-1/2}>0$ and the representatives just defined, one has
$|Y_{l,-m}|=|Y_{lm}|$ and
$\overline{Y_{lm}}=(-1)^mY_{l,-m}$ for all $l$ and all $m$ with $|m|\le l$;

(d) the family $\{Y_{lm}:l\ge0,\ -l\le m\le l\}$ is orthonormal in $L^2(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$
([[def-inner-product-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]): for all $(l,m)\ne(l',m')$
with $|m|\le l$, $|m'|\le l'$, the integral $\int_{S^2}Y_{lm}\overline{Y_{l'm'}}\,d\sigma$ equals $0$, and it
equals $1$ when $(l,m)=(l',m')$;

(e) $w_{l0}=P_l$, and $w_{ll}(t)=(-1)^l\frac{(2l)!}{2^l l!}(1-t^2)^{l/2}$.

The functions $Y_{lm}$ are complex-valued $L^2$-functions on the sphere; no physical interpretation as angular
momentum eigenfunctions or spherical harmonics of an atom is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]],
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let

$$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$

and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set
([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then:

(a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$,
$$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$
the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle;

(b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$;

(c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue
integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and
imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

Let $a < b$ be reals, let $G : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at every
point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ ([[def-derivative]]; at $a$ and $b$
this is the one-sided derivative), let $f := G'$, and suppose $f$ is integrable
on $[a,b]$ ([[def-darboux-integral]]). Then

$$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**Both hypotheses are needed and neither is removable.** A function may be
differentiable everywhere with $G'$ not integrable — then the left-hand side does
not exist (an everywhere differentiable function with unbounded derivative) — and an
integrable $f$ need not be the derivative of anything
(the sign function); both witnesses are on the
companion page.

**No continuity of $f$ is assumed**, which is what makes this the working form:
the theorem evaluates $\int_a^b f$ for every integrable derivative, not only for
continuous integrands.

For all real $x,y$,
$$\sin(x+y)=\sin x\cos y+\cos x\sin y,$$
$$\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.$$

For $x\in\mathbb R$, define
$$\sin x:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!},\qquad\cos x:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n}}{(2n)!}.$$

These are real power series in the sense of [[def-real-power-series-and-radius-of-convergence]]. Their convergence for every real argument is discharged by [[lem-sine-and-cosine-series-converge-everywhere]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Use the notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-strongly-continuous-rotation-action]]: $S^2$, the polar measure $\sigma$ with
$\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, the Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$, the complete orthonormal family $(Y_{lm})$, the blocks
$V_l$, the finite span $H$, the spaces $H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of complex harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree
$l$, the restriction maps $\mathrm{res}_l$, and the unitary action $U(R)F=\text{class of }\tilde F(R^{-1}\cdot)$
of $SO(3)$. Fix $\hbar>0$ and for $i=1,2,3$ define the rotation matrices
$$R_1(t):=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&\cos t&-\sin t\\0&\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_2(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&0&\sin t\\0&1&0\\-\sin t&0&\cos t\end{pmatrix},\quad R_3(t):=\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&-\sin t&0\\ \sin t&\cos t&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},$$
put $U_i(t):=U(R_i(t))$. Let $L_z$ denote the diagonal operator of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]], set $S:=R_2(-\pi/2)$, $W:=R_1(\pi/2)$,
and define
$$L_3:=L_z,\qquad L_1:=U(S)^{-1}L_zU(S),\qquad L_2:=U(W)^{-1}L_zU(W),$$
with domains $D(L_1)=U(S)^{-1}D(L_z)$, $D(L_2)=U(W)^{-1}D(L_z)$ and $D(L_3)=D(L_z)$.
Here $e^{-itL_z/\hbar}$ is the explicit diagonal unitary sending $Y_{lm}$ to $e^{-itm}Y_{lm}$;
$e^{-itL_1/\hbar}$ and $e^{-itL_2/\hbar}$ mean its conjugates by $U(S)$ and $U(W)$, respectively.
The proof identifies these operators with the complete strong derivative generators, so this construction
has the same generator meaning without an appeal to an unrestricted spectral or Stone theorem. For a polynomial $p$ put
$$D_ip:=(x\times\nabla p)_i=\sum_{j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\,x_j\,\partial_kp,$$
where $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is the sign of the permutation $(1,2,3)\mapsto(i,j,k)$ and is $0$ when two indices
coincide. Then:

(a) each $L_i$ is a self-adjoint operator on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ with $U(R_i(t))=e^{-itL_i/\hbar}$ for all real
$t$; the finite span $H$ is contained in $D(L_i)$ and is a core of $L_i$
([[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);
and for $F\in V_l$ with polynomial representative $p_F\in H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ one has
$$L_iF=\mathrm{res}_l(-i\hbar\,D_ip_F),$$
that is, $(L_iF)(\Omega)=-i\hbar\,D_ip_F(\Omega)$ for $\sigma$-almost every $\Omega\in S^2$; in particular
$L_iY_{lm}\in V_l$ for all $l,m$ and $L_iH\subseteq H$;

(b) on $H$ the operators satisfy the commutation relations
$$L_iL_j-L_jL_i=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}L_k;$$

(c) $L_3=L_z$ as self-adjoint operators (equal domains and equal action); in particular $L_3Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$, so that
$L_3$ is diagonal in the basis $(Y_{lm})$, and for every $F\in H$ and chart point $(\theta,\varphi)$ one has $(L_3F)(\theta,\varphi)=-i\hbar\,\partial_\varphi F(\theta,\varphi)$;

(d) rotational conjugation identifies the domains: with the two quarter-turn rotations
$S:=R_2(-\pi/2)$ and $W:=R_1(\pi/2)$ one has
$$U(S)L_1U(S)^{-1}=L_3,\qquad U(W)L_2U(W)^{-1}=L_3,$$
as self-adjoint operators, and consequently $U(S)D(L_1)=D(L_3)$ and $U(W)D(L_2)=D(L_3)$: the three domains
are unitarily identified.

All assertions are mathematical statements about operators on $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$; no physical interpretation of
the generators as angular momentum is asserted, and no measurement postulate is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the

[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]: $S^2$ with its

([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-inner-product-space]]), the complete orthonormal

([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks
$V_{l}:=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$, the finite span $H$,
the self-adjoint operators $L_{1},L_{2},L_{3}$ with $L_{3}=L_{z}$ and
$L_{i}Y_{lm}\in V_{l}$ for all $l,m,i$, and the diagonal sphere Laplacian $A$
with $AY_{lm}=l(l+1)Y_{lm}$. Then for every $l\ge0$:

(a) each $L_{i}$ leaves $V_{l}$ invariant, and the restriction
$L_{i}|_{V_{l}}$ is a self-adjoint endomorphism of the finite-dimensional
inner product space $V_{l}$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), with
$L_{3}Y_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$ for $-l\le m\le l$;

(b) the triple $\bigl((1/\hbar)L_{1}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{2}|_{V_{l}},(1/\hbar)L_{3}|_{V_{l}}\bigr)$

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
internal-factor assignment of the spin postulate P6, read for the massive
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and
the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $l\ge0$, $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$, a unit vector
$w\in\mathbb C^{r}$ and a complex-valued $R\in C_{c}^{\infty}((0,\infty))$, and
let $h_{lm}$ be the harmonic homogeneous polynomial of degree $l$ with
$h_{lm}|_{S^2}=Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]] clause (c)
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]]). Define
the model vector
$$\psi(x):=R(|x|)\,h_{lm}(x)\,w\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^{3},\ x\ne0),\qquad \psi(0):=0 .$$
Then:

(a) $\psi$ is a well-defined class in the model's state space $H_{s}$ and in
fact $\psi\in C_{c}^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})\subseteq\mathcal
S^{(r)}$; it lies in $D(L_{i})$ for each $i$, and for $x\ne0$
$$(L_{i}\psi)(x)=R(|x|)\,\bigl(-i\hbar\,D_{i}h_{lm}\bigr)(x)\,w,\qquad D_{i}h_{lm}=(x\times\nabla h_{lm})_{i},$$
so that $-i\hbar D_{i}h_{lm}$ is the polynomial representative of the sphere
function $L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]]; in particular
$L_{3}\psi=\hbar m\,\psi$;

(b) with $\|R\|_{l}^{2}:=\int_{0}^{\infty}|R(r)|^{2}r^{2l+2}\,dr$ one has
$\|\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}$ and
$$\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\|R\|_{l}^{2}\,\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{3}\|L_{i}\psi\|^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)\,\|\psi\|^{2},$$
so the Casimir quadratic form of the model's orbital generators on $\psi$
takes the value $\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$;

(c) consequently, for the pure preparation of the unit vector
$\psi/\|\psi\|$ (for $R\not\equiv0$), the mean and the second moment of the
outcome law of $(L_{3},\mathrm{J\,s})$ are finite and equal
$\hbar m$ and $\hbar^{2}m^{2}$, so the variance vanishes; for each $i$ the
mean and second moment of the law of $L_{i}$ are finite and the second moment
equals $\bigl\|L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{lm}\bigr\|^{2}$; the model reads $(l,m)$
as the **orbital angular momentum quantum numbers** of the preparation, in
the sense of the eigenvalue of the angular momentum-squared form and the
eigenvalue of $L_{3}$;

(d) **Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P5, P6
and the cited mathematics, and concern the spatial factor of the massive
model. The item asserts no dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no
joint sharp values of two different components $L_{i},L_{j}$, no empirical
value and no spectral resolution of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$: the identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)$ is a quadratic-form statement on the
displayed smooth vectors and is not read as a statement about a self-adjoint
operator $\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}$ on the full spatial Hilbert space.

derivations.claim: [Low polynomials] Substituting the constants of [F1] gives $h_{00}=2^{-1/2}(2\pi)^{-1/2}=(4\pi)^{-1/2}$, $h_{10}=\sqrt{3/2}(2\pi)^{-1/2}x_{3}=\sqrt{3/(4\pi)}x_{3}$, and $h_{1,\pm1}=\mp\sqrt{3/4}(2\pi)^{-1/2}(x_{1}\pm ix_{2})=\mp\sqrt{3/(8\pi)}(x_{1}\pm ix_{2})$, which are the displayed polynomials of (i); each is harmonic and homogeneous of the stated degree by [F1].

[Sphere norms and orthogonality] By [F2] and step 1.1, $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{00}|^{2}d\sigma=\frac{1}{4\pi}\cdot4\pi=1$; $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{10}|^{2}d\sigma=\frac{3}{4\pi}\int\Omega_{3}^{2}d\sigma=\frac{3}{4\pi}\cdot\frac{4\pi}{3}=1$; and $\int_{S^{2}}|Y_{1,\pm1}|^{2}d\sigma=\frac{3}{8\pi}\int(\Omega_{1}^{2}+\Omega_{2}^{2})d\sigma=\frac{3}{8\pi}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}=1$. The mixed products with $Y_{00}$ integrate to zero: $\Omega_1$ and $\Omega_2$ have zero $\varphi$-integrals, while $\int_0^\pi\cos\theta\sin\theta\,d\theta=0$ for $\Omega_3$, by the angle formula and the trigonometric primitives in [F2]. The mixed products of $Y_{10}$ with $Y_{1,\pm1}$ vanish by $\int\Omega_3\Omega_1\,d\sigma=\int\Omega_3\Omega_2\,d\sigma=0$ from [F2]. Finally, $Y_{11}\overline{Y_{1,-1}}=-\frac{3}{8\pi}(\Omega_1^2-\Omega_2^2+2i\Omega_1\Omega_2)$ has zero integral because [F2] gives equal second moments for $\Omega_1,\Omega_2$ and a zero cross moment; the reversed mixed integrals are their complex conjugates. Hence the four functions are orthonormal.

[Degree-one eigenvalues] By step 1.1, direct differentiation gives $D_{3}h_{1m}=(x_{1}\partial_{2}-x_{2}\partial_{1})h_{1m}=im\,h_{1m}$ for $m=-1,0,1$, hence $-i\hbar D_{3}h_{1m}=\hbar m h_{1m}$ as a polynomial identity; restricting to the sphere and using [F3] gives $L_{3}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{1m}=\hbar mY_{1m}$. The Casimir identity of [F3] with $l=1$ gives $\sum_{i}(L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}})^{2}F=2\hbar^{2}F$ for $F\in V_{1}$. For $l=0$, each $D_{i}h_{00}=0$, so [F3] gives $L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}}Y_{00}=0$ and therefore $\sum_{i}(L_{i}^{\mathrm{sph}})^{2}Y_{00}=0$. This proves (ii).
[General case] Clause (iii) restates [F4] in the normalization $\|Y_{lm}\|=1$; combining it with step 2.2 gives the low-degree instances, completing the verification of (i)-(iii).

citations.quote:
Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s$, together with the effective magnetic-moment coupling
adopted in [[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] and the
angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]], and
assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Fix a real constant
$B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and use the uniform static field profile
$\mathbf B(x):=(0,0,B_{z})$, so that the Zeeman energy operator of the
postulate is
$$H_{Z}=H_{0}-\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3},\qquad H_{0}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
with flow $U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$, and put $\omega:=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$
with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. For a unit vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ put
$\psi(t):=U_{Z}(t)\psi$ and $\langle S_{i}\rangle(t):=\langle
S_{i}\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$. Then:

(a) $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{Z})$ and
$$U_{Z}(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\,e^{it\gamma_{s}B_{z}S_{3}/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
so in particular the transverse means satisfy, for every $t$,
$$\langle S_{1}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0)+\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0),\qquad \langle S_{2}\rangle(t)=\cos(\omega t)\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)-\sin(\omega t)\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),$$
and the transverse vector $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(t),\langle S_{2}\rangle(t)\bigr)$
is the rotation of $\bigl(\langle S_{1}\rangle(0),\langle S_{2}\rangle(0)\bigr)$
by the angle $-\omega t$ in the $(1,2)$-plane;

(b) the component along the field is conserved: $S_{3}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S_{3}$
and $\langle S_{3}\rangle(t)=\langle S_{3}\rangle(0)$ for every unit $\psi$
and every $t$; more generally the outcome law of $S_{3}$ is time-independent
in every preparation;

(c) the conjugation identities
$$e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{1}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{1}+\sin(\omega t)S_{2},\qquad e^{itH_{Z}/\hbar}S_{2}e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}=\cos(\omega t)S_{2}-\sin(\omega t)S_{1}$$
hold as bounded operator identities, and with $S^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$
(the Casimir operator of the model) also $S^{2}U_{Z}(t)=U_{Z}(t)S^{2}$;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling; it concerns the uniform static field $\mathbf B=(0,0,B_{z})$
with $B_{z}\in\mathbb R$ and the declared isolated model. It excludes
inhomogeneous and time-dependent fields, spin-dependent spatial potentials,
radiation, relaxation and environment coupling, asserts no measured
precession frequency and no measured gyromagnetic parameter, and identifies
no apparatus: $\omega=\gamma_{s}B_{z}$ is a model quantity computed from
assigned model parameters.

Adopt as a physical assumption of the framework, for the declared massive
spin-$s$ particle model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] and only within the
scope stated below, the following **effective magnetic-moment coupling**
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]).

**(i) Gyromagnetic parameter and magnetic moment.** For the declared spin
label $s$ assign a real **gyromagnetic parameter** $\gamma_{s}$, with unit
$\mathrm{s^{-1}\,T^{-1}}$, and define the **magnetic moment** of the model as
the internal-factor operator
$$\boldsymbol\mu:=\gamma_{s}\mathbf S=(\gamma_{s}S_{1},\gamma_{s}S_{2},\gamma_{s}S_{3}),$$
with unit $\mathrm{J\,T^{-1}}$. Here $\mathbf S=(S_{1},S_{2},S_{3})$ are the
spin operators of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] read on
the internal factor as in
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause (c). The
parameter $\gamma_{s}$ is an empirical model parameter of the species: it is
part of the declared model data, with uncertainty, and it is not derived from
$s$, from the mass parameter $m$ or from the charge of the particle; no
relation between $\gamma_{s}$ and any other species parameter is asserted by
this postulate.

**(ii) Prescribed field and Zeeman energy operator.** Let
$\mathbf B:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R^{3}$ be a real bounded measurable
vector field, the **prescribed magnetic field profile**, with components
$B_{i}$ in tesla, entering the model as externally prescribed data
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]); in the
declared inertial frame the model adopts the **Zeeman energy operator**
$$H_{Z}:=H_{0}+M_{W},\qquad H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2},\qquad M_{W}f:=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\gamma_{s}B_{i}(\cdot)\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)(\cdot),$$
on the componentwise domain
$D(H_{Z}):=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, the domain of $H_{0}$
(componentwise, [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]];
$\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ is the componentwise free operator with that domain by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) applied to each component). The added term $M_{W}$ is bounded with
$\|M_{W}\|\le|\gamma_{s}|\sum_{i}\|B_{i}\|_{\infty}\max_{i}\|S_{i}\|$, so
$H_{Z}$ is a bounded self-adjoint perturbation of $H_{0}$ on the unchanged
domain, with unit joule, and the assignment $t\mapsto e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}$ is
a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group read in the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). The profile
$\mathbf B$ is a model input; the items of this page assert neither the
Maxwell equations nor a source or boundary realization of $\mathbf B$, and
the boundedness of $\mathbf B$ is an explicit hypothesis, not a general
property of magnetic fields.

**(iii) What is assumed and what is not.** (a) The coupling
$-\boldsymbol\mu\cdot\mathbf B(Q)$ is an **effective interaction**: it is
adopted, not derived from the spin representation P6, from the
minimal-coupling postulate P5a of the framework or from classical
electromagnetism. (b) No value of $\gamma_{s}$ and no comparison with
measured gyromagnetic ratios or $g$-factors is made here. (c) No spin-orbit
coupling, no fine or hyperfine structure, no relativistic correction and no
radiation reaction is included. (d) A time-dependent field profile requires
its own domain and evolution hypotheses and is outside this postulate. (e)
The internal factor is not a spatial current distribution and $\boldsymbol\mu$
is not asserted to arise from a rotating charge distribution.

(iv) **Status.** This postulate is an adopted model assumption with the
physical scope above; it is motivated by and formulated after the cited
sources, which treat the coupling as a model input, and no deduction of it
from the framework's other postulates is claimed.

**(a) Assigned energy observable.** Adopt the autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4) for a declared isolated system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned energy observable** of the system is an assigned sharp observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ in the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), whose declared unit $u_H$ is an energy unit in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (joules in the SI conventions fixed there). Thus $H_{\mathrm{op}}:D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subset H\to H$ is densely defined and self-adjoint ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]), with spectral projection-valued measure $E_H$ on the Borel sets of $\mathbb R$ under the choice hypotheses of [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and its outcome law in a preparation is the law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). The assignment of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is part of the model specification, as in clause (i) of P4; this definition asserts nothing about which laboratory quantity of a concrete system realizes it.

**(b) The unitary flow.** The **time evolution** or **flow** of the isolated system is the family
$$U(t):=\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tH_{\mathrm{op}}\Bigr):=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_H(\lambda)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P4 in the spectral calculus of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); here $\hbar>0$ is the reduced Planck constant with its value and unit fixed by [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], so that $tH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ is dimensionless. Equivalently, $U(t)=e^{itT}$ for the self-adjoint generator $T:=-H_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar$ with $D(T)=D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$; the two readings agree by the uniqueness of the generator in Stone's theorem, and by [[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]] ([[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-flow-calculus]] clause (a)) the family $U$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: $U(0)=I$, $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$, $U(t)^{*}=U(t)^{-1}=U(-t)$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]).

**(c) Schroedinger picture.** The **Schroedinger-picture evolution** of a preparation is fixed by clause (iii) of P4. A state vector evolves by $\psi(t):=U(t)\psi(0)$ for every $\psi(0)\in H$, and the **state at time $t$** of the pure preparation $[\psi(0)]$ is the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$, which is well defined because $U(t)$ is injective; a general preparation $\rho$, that is an element of the state space $D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], evolves by
$$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*},$$
the reading of clause (iii) of P4 in the density-operator vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]). In this picture the assigned observables are held fixed at their assigned values and the preparation moves.

**(d) Heisenberg picture.** For a **bounded** assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ — that is, an assigned sharp observable with $A\in\mathcal B(H)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), so that $A$ is self-adjoint and everywhere defined — the **Heisenberg representative** of $(A,u_A)$ at time $t$ is the pair $(A_H(t),u_A)$ with the same declared unit and
$$A_H(t):=U(t)^{*}AU(t)=U(-t)AU(t).$$
By [[lem-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-flow]] clauses (a) and (d), $A_H(t)$ is again bounded and self-adjoint with spectral projection-valued measure $E_{A_H(t)}(B)=U(-t)E_A(B)U(t)$, so $(A_H(t),u_A)$ is again an assigned sharp observable of the framework; in this picture the preparation is held fixed at its value at time $0$ and the observables move. The two pictures are two bookkeeping devices for the same model; the statement that they assign the same outcome laws is proved in the Heisenberg-picture theorem of this page, not assumed here.

**(e) Stationary preparations.** A preparation $\rho\in D(H)$ is **stationary** for the assigned energy observable when $\rho(t)=\rho$ for every $t\in\mathbb R$. A pure preparation $[\psi]$ is stationary when $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for every $t$, that is, when the evolved vector remains in the ray of $\psi$; the characterization of this condition by the eigenrays of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ is proved in the stationary-states theorem of this page, not assumed here. An **energy eigenstate** is a pure preparation of a unit eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$, and a **stationary state** in the model is a stationary pure preparation; by that theorem the two notions coincide.

**(f) Energy-compatible observables.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ is **compatible with the energy**, or **energy-compatible**, when its spectral projection-valued measure and that of the energy commute strongly,
$$E_A(B)E_H(C)=E_H(C)E_A(B)\qquad\text{for all Borel }B,C\subseteq\mathbb R .$$
This is an equality of bounded operators on $H$, not a relation between formal commutators on a small domain; the phrase **conserved quantity** for an energy-compatible assigned observable is a claim about the time invariance of its outcome law and is established in the energy-conservation theorem of this page for bounded $A$.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P4 together with P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P4, P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematics, assert no dynamics for a prescribed time-dependent family or for an open system (clauses (iv) and (v) of P4 are separate model assumptions treated on their own pages), assert no measurement model, no apparatus realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any laboratory system is exactly isolated.

**(a) State space.** Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] for a declared system of the declared massive-matter sector, with its assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. The **state space of the system in the model** is the set
$$D(H)=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}$$
of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]: the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators on $H$ of trace one. A **state** of the system is an element of $D(H)$; this is the geometry vocabulary for the general preparations of clause (iii) of the state postulate. The model's adopted assignment of a state to each preparation is not produced by this definition; it is the content of that postulate.

**(b) Pure and mixed states.** A state is **pure** when it is one of the operators $T_{u,u}$ with $u\in S(H)$, and **mixed** when it is not pure, as in [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the map
$$j:R(H)\to D(H),\qquad j([\psi])=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
is a bijection of the ray space onto the set of pure states; and by clause (ii) of the state postulate the pure preparations are the unit rays of $H$, so the model's pure preparations are exactly its pure states.

**(c) State assigned to a state vector.** For a nonzero vector $\psi\in H^{\times}$ the **state assigned to $\psi$** is the normalized rank-one operator
$$\widehat\rho(\psi)=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}\in D(H),$$
which by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] depends only on the ray $[\psi]$; clause (ii) of the state postulate assigns the same operator to the pure preparation $[\psi]$. The zero vector is excluded here because $\|\psi\|^{-1}$ is defined only for $\psi\ne0$; no state is assigned to it, in agreement with the state postulate.

**(d) Mixtures and purity.** A **statistical mixture** of preparations with weights is the trace-norm convergent sum of clause (iii) of the state postulate; its value is the corresponding convex combination of states. The **purity** of a state $\rho$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})$, and by [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]] a state is pure exactly when its purity equals $1$.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) record the readings of the state postulate in the geometry vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. The cited mathematical suppliers of the ray-to-state correspondence and of the purity criterion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is carried as a hypothesis of these readings. They adopt no assumption beyond the state postulate and that hypothesis, assert no dynamics, no probability law and no measurement model, and make no empirical claim: in particular, whether a given laboratory preparation is pure or mixed, and whether a given apparatus realizes a prescribed mixture, are physical identifications with uncertainty, governed by the preparation and apparatus assumptions of the framework, not consequences of this definition. Superselection restrictions and identical-particle symmetry sectors, where imposed, are separate assumptions by clause (v) of the state postulate and are not part of the state space fixed here.

Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}=0$ when two of $i,j,k$ coincide, and otherwise $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ is the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$; the sum ranges over $k\in\{x,y,z\}$. The same convention with indices $1,2,3$ uses the order-preserving relabelling $(1,2,3)=(x,y,z)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor
assignment of the identical-particle and spin postulate P6, all read for the
spin-$s$ model of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with
mass parameter $m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and
$r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Let
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the model's state space with
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$, and let $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ be its
componentwise Schwartz class
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]). Units are
those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the unit of angular
momentum is the unit of action (J$\,$s).

**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,
$$L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clause (b),
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

**(c) Spin angular momentum.** Let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the internal
operators of [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] clause
(c), the matrix actions $\bigl(S_{i}f\bigr)_{l}=\hbar\sum_{m}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}$
of the self-adjoint matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]. The model reads
$(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the $i$-th **spin
angular momentum**; on the internal factor,
$$[S_{i},S_{j}]=i\hbar\sum_{k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}S_{k},\qquad S^{2}:=S_{x}^{2}+S_{y}^{2}+S_{z}^{2}=\hbar^{2}s(s+1)I$$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a),(b),(c),
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)). The
**ladder** operators $S_{\pm}:=S_{x}\pm iS_{y}$ and the finite projections on
the basis vectors $e_{m}$ are structural objects of the internal factor, not
assigned sharp observables, and $S_{\pm}$ are not self-adjoint. For $s=\tfrac12$
one has $S_{i}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_{i}$ in the Pauli matrices
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)). The internal
factor is a finite-dimensional bookkeeping factor: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Total angular momentum.** For each $i$ let
$$J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}:=L_{i}+S_{i},\qquad D(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}):=D(L_{i}),$$
the self-adjoint sum of
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clause (c)
(well defined because $S_{i}$ is bounded and strongly commutes with $L_{i}$;
[[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-product-flow-generator]] clause (a),
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). The model reads
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an assigned sharp observable, the
$i$-th **total angular momentum**; its flow is the coordinate subgroup
$t\mapsto U_{s}(A_{i}(t))$ of the lifted rotation action, using the physical-axes cover $\rho(W)=C^{-1}\rho_0(W)C$ defined in that lemma (rather than the literal quaternion-coordinate cover $\rho_0$),
$U_{s}(A_{i}(t))=e^{-itJ_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-su2-lift-of-the-rotation-action]] clauses (b),(c)).

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the angular momentum vocabulary
of this page within P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited readings. No new
physical assumption is added; in particular no magnetic coupling, no
spin-orbit interaction, no SU(2) gauge structure and no anomaly is
introduced. Whether a laboratory angular momentum measurement is described by
one of the assigned pairs $(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$, $(S_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ or
$(J_{i}^{\mathrm{tot}},\mathrm{J\,s})$ is a tested identification with
uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not a
consequence of this definition; no measurement procedure, apparatus,
resolution or empirical value is supplied here. Antiunitary symmetries,
superselection rules and symmetries of preparations as opposed to dynamics
are outside the definition.

Let $X$ be a real or complex Banach space and let $A\in\mathcal B(X)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). For $t\in\mathbb R$ define $E(t):=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{t^n}{n!}A^n$. Then the series converges absolutely in the operator norm $\|\cdot\|$ of $\mathcal B(X)$, uniformly for $t$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R$; $E(t)\in\mathcal B(X)$ with $\|E(t)\| \le e^{|t|\|A\|}$; $E(0)=I$ and $E(t+s)=E(t)E(s)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$; $t\mapsto E(t)$ is of class $C^\infty$ in the operator norm with $$E'(t)=AE(t)=E(t)A,$$ and $\|E(t)-I-tA\| \le\frac{t^2}{2}\|A\|^2e^{|t|\|A\|}$, so that $\frac{E(t)-I}{t}\to A$ in operator norm as $t\to0$. In particular $E$ is a uniformly continuous (hence strongly continuous) group of bounded operators on $X$ whose generator is the bounded operator $A$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The
**operator norm** of $T$ is

$$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$

The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it
above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound
property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]).
In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a
member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice
principle is used for this assertion.

The same number is the least bound of $T$:

$$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$

If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives

$$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$

When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$,
so $\|T\| = 0$.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

derivations.claim: [Sector identities] By [F2] one has $S_{3}(f\otimes e_{\pm})=\pm\frac{\hbar}{2}f\otimes e_{\pm}$ and $H_{0}$ acts on the spatial factor only; hence, for $f\in D(H_{0})$, $H_{Z}(f\otimes e_{\pm})=(H_{0}f)\otimes e_{\pm}\mp\frac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}f\otimes e_{\pm}$, and taking the inner product with the unit vector $f\otimes e_{\pm}$ gives the displayed expectation. For every $f\in L^{2}$, not necessarily in $D(H_{0})$, [F1] gives the product-flow identity, with $e^{it\gamma B_zS_3/\hbar}e_\pm=e^{\pm i\gamma B_zt/2}e_\pm$ by [F2]; the transverse means then precess as in the cited theorem, proving (i).

[Toy levels and evolution] In the two-dimensional internal model with free part $E_{0}I$, the operator $H_{Z}^{(2)}=E_{0}I-\gamma B_{z}S_{3}$ is diagonal in $(e_{+},e_{-})$ with entries $E_{0}\mp\frac{\gamma\hbar B_{z}}{2}$ by [F2], so its eigenvalues are those entries and the signed difference is $\gamma\hbar B_{z}=\hbar\omega$; by [F3] the exponential is the displayed diagonal unitary, and the relative phase accumulates at the angular frequency $\omega$, which is (ii).

[Conjugation identities] With $V(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}^{(2)}/\hbar}e^{itE_{0}/\hbar}=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\omega t/2},e^{-i\omega t/2})$ from step 2.1, direct matrix multiplication using [F2] gives $V(t)^{*}\sigma_{1}V(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&e^{-i\omega t}\\ e^{i\omega t}&0\end{pmatrix}=\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{1}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{2}$ and $V(t)^{*}\sigma_{2}V(t)=\begin{pmatrix}0&-ie^{-i\omega t}\\ ie^{i\omega t}&0\end{pmatrix}=\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{2}-\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{1}$, which is (iii) and agrees with the general conjugation of [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-zeeman-precession]] clause (c).

[Scope] Since $H_{Z}^{(2)}$ is diagonal in $(e_{+},e_{-})$, its evolution multiplies the two amplitudes by phases and preserves the sector weights $|c_{\pm}|^{2}$: no spin flip occurs without a driving term, and the truncation was an explicit toy assumption, which is (iv).

The internal space is two-dimensional and the truncated model is the 2×2 operator H_Z^{(2)} of steps 2.1 and 3.1.

The precession matrices of step 3.1 are evaluated for all t, including t=0 where they reduce to the identity.
The statement assumes the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice; the flow and conservation suppliers used in steps 1.1 and 2.1 rest on them.

Corrected the sector multiplier to exp(+/-i gamma B_z t/2), since energies have the opposite signs. Specified E0 as real energy in joules, making the toy Hamiltonian Hermitian. Its diagonal evolution has a changing relative phase at signed omega when both amplitudes are nonzero, while sector weights stay fixed; removed the contradictory stationary-relative-phase claim. Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability
postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4, the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and the internal-factor assignment of the
spin postulate P6, read for the massive spin-$\tfrac12$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$ and spin label $s=\tfrac12$, together with the effective
magnetic-moment coupling of
[[post-nrqm-angular-momentum-magnetic-moment-coupling]] with parameter
$\gamma_{1/2}\in\mathbb R$ and the angular momentum readings of
[[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom
of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-countable-choice]]). Let $B_{z}\in C^{1}(\mathbb R)$ be real with
$B_{z}$ and $B_{z}'$ bounded, let
$$\mathbf B(x):=\bigl(0,0,B_{z}(x_{1})\bigr),$$
let $H_{Z}$ be the Zeeman operator of the magnetic-moment postulate for this
profile, acting on $H_{1/2}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$ with domain
$D(H_{Z})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2})$, and let $u(t)=e^{-itH_{Z}/\hbar}u_{0}$
be its flow. Identify $H_{1/2}$ with
$\mathcal H=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\oplus L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
through the internal basis $(e_{1/2},e_{-1/2})$, and let $P_{+}:=\tfrac12(I+2S_{3}/\hbar)$
be the fibrewise orthogonal projection onto the spin-up line $e_{1/2}$.
Then:

(a) under this identification $H_{Z}$ is the operator
$$K(u_{+},u_{-})=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{+}-\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{+},\ \frac{1}{2m}\sum_{j}P_{j}^{2}u_{-}+\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}B_{z}(Q_{x})u_{-}\Bigr),\qquad D(K)=W^{2,2}\oplus W^{2,2},$$
of [[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-conditional-stern-gerlach-force]] with
$\gamma_{s}:=\gamma_{1/2}$; consequently $H_{Z}$ is self-adjoint,
$S_{3}H_{Z}=H_{Z}S_{3}$ on $D(H_{Z})$, the sector weights
$\|P_{\pm}u(t)\|^{2}$ and the mean $\langle S_{3}\rangle_{u(t)}$ are

(b) if in addition $u_{0}\in D(H_{Z}^{2})$ is a unit vector with
$P_{+}u_{0}=u_{0}$ and $B_{z}'(x_{1})=G$ for every $x_{1}$ in a Borel set
$N\subseteq\mathbb R$ satisfying
$\int_{\mathbb R\setminus N}\eta_{+}(x_{1})\,dx_{1}=0$, where
$\eta_{+}(x_{1}):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|u_{0}^{+}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3})|^{2}\,dx_{2}\,dx_{3}$
is the first-coordinate marginal density of the spin-up component, then
$$\frac{d}{dt}\Bigr|_{t=0}\bigl\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\bigr\rangle=\frac{\gamma_{1/2}\hbar}{2}\,G ;$$
for $t\ne0$ the general rate is
$\frac{d}{dt}\langle P_{x}u(t),u(t)\rangle=\gamma_{1/2}\langle S_{3}B_{z}'(Q_{x})u(t),u(t)\rangle$;

(c) the profile satisfies $\operatorname{div}\mathbf B=0$ and
$\operatorname{curl}\mathbf B=(0,-B_{z}'(x_{1}),0)$ at every point of
$\mathbb R^{3}$, as identities of the displayed components;

(d) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P6 and the
adopted coupling. Clause (b) is a model prediction for the rate of the mean
transverse momentum of a prepared spin-up state under the marginal-support
hypothesis; it is not an observation of a beam splitting, a trajectory or a
count, it identifies no apparatus, calibration or detector, and it asserts

The word "Stern-Gerlach" names this conditional model, not a reported
experiment; no measured value of $\gamma_{1/2}$ enters and no empirical
